final_candidates.decision_summary: Q488 (verified WT residue) borders the m102.4 epitope region near the receptor-binding domain; introducing arginine can disrupt antibody paratope contacts while lying outside the core ephrin-B2/B3 contact footprint. Moderate confidence due to lack of epitope-mapping evidence.

K489 is adjacent to Q488 in the same antibody-accessible surface patch; a lysine-to-asparagine change can subtly alter local topology and potential glycosylation while posing low folding/receptor-binding risk. Effect on m102.4 escape is likely modest.

E483 is a verified surface-exposed acidic residue in the epitope-proximal region; a charge-reversal substitution is a classic immune-escape strategy with low stability cost. Its distance from the antibody core contact lowers confidence in escape potency.

stop_reason.detail: Numbering verification was completed and no external evidence is available in this condition, so further self-iteration cannot improve the Top-3.

history.rationale: Lys509 lies adjacent to the ephrin-binding pocket in the G head domain and is within the described m102.4 footprint; a charge reversal can disrupt antibody contact while leaving the hydrophobic core of the receptor-binding site intact.
K509 lies near the m102.4 epitope but outside the core ephrin-B2/B3 contact footprint; charge reversal is a classic antibody-escape move with low folding risk.
Residue 516 sits on the solvent-exposed rim of the receptor-binding face; a conservative polar substitution can alter antibody paratope contacts with minimal impact on ephrin-B2/B3 binding.
I516 is in an antibody-accessible surface patch; a conservative polar substitution is less likely to destabilize than a large charge change.

Q488 is near a loop bordering the m102.4 epitope; substituting a larger charged residue can sterically and electrostatically interfere with antibody binding without touching core receptor-contact residues.
Q488 borders the m102.4 footprint; arginine could disrupt antibody contact but may sit closer to receptor-binding residues, so confidence is moderate.
Asn510 neighbors receptor-pocket residues and can introduce a negative charge that weakens antibody interaction while preserving the local backbone conformation needed for ephrin binding.
N510 is adjacent to K509 in the same epitope patch; glycosylation-site loss or charge change could impair antibody binding, though N-linked glycan loss may slightly reduce shielding.
T501 is on the epitope periphery; removal of the hydroxyl can reduce antibody hydrogen bonding with only minor effects on the receptor-binding surface.
T501A is a small, low-risk change but may have weak effect on m102.4 binding; retained as backup.
Charge neutralization at K489 may reduce electrostatic complementarity to m102.4 while conserving side-chain size in a peripheral epitope position.
Adjacent to Q488; a K-to-N change is mild and may be too conservative to confer escape.
A charge flip at E483, distal to the central receptor-contact residues, may perturb antibody approach geometry while preserving overall fold and receptor binding.
Charge-reversal escape logic is sound but E483 is farther from the receptor-binding pocket, so escape probability is uncertain.
Position 515 is on the pocket rim; reversing the charge can destabilize antibody binding while the conservative size change limits risk to ephrin engagement.
Near I516 in a putative epitope-adjacent patch; charge reversal may alter antibody contact but risk to local structure is higher.
K460 borders the receptor-binding region; a charge flip could reduce antibody affinity but carries moderate risk of affecting nearby receptor-binding geometry.
K460 is likely distant from the m102.4 epitope and charge reversal there is more likely to affect stability than escape.

rejection.reason: K460 is likely distant from the m102.4 epitope and charge reversal there is more likely to affect stability than escape.

history.rationale: A conservative substitution near the epitope edge; effect on escape is likely modest but structural risk to receptor binding is low.
